titleStmt.title: The Tsungli Yamen to Mr. Conger.

head.hi: The Tsungli Yamen to Mr. Conger.

div.p: “The Boxers and the Christians do not get on together. I have again and again admonished them to make peace with each other, and the Boxers have gradually returned to their homes. I learn that while some of the Boxers were returning to their homes they passed through the Han-chuang (village), in the district of Yu Cheng. The Christians had set an ambush there and attacked the Boxers with rapid-firing guns, resulting in ten and more persons being killed. The Christians stole their ponies. In order to ascertain whether this report was true or not, I was just on the point of investigating the affair when I received from the magistrate of Yu Cheng, Mr. Hsiang, a petition setting forth in the general similar representations to what I had heard. A feeling of ill will has been contracted among these people which is becoming more intense every day, and from this time on the Boxers may again congregate together, and (that) in the future they will seek their revenge is a matter that can not be avoided.”

In sending this note to your excellency for your information, we ask that you will instruct the Christians of said place that they must not make trouble out of nothing, in order that cordial good feeling may prevail among the people and themselves.
